data.narrative:
Long Wall is a late-stage Defense & Security company founded by Dan Piemont and Harry O'Hanley (both ex-SpaceX and ex-Morgan Stanley) that has raised $544M to date. The valuation universe includes 2 public comparables and 8 private peers, notably Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems, though a sufficiently narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier does not exist.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and anchors the analysis. Using total capital raised ($544M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Late Stage progression yields $653M. The Peer-Median method is not applicable; while 23 same-sector peers exist in Defense & Security, filtering to same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier comparables yields fewer than 3 datapoints, insufficient for reliable triangulation without risking material distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $555M (low) to $751M (median to high), centered on $653M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty regarding appropriate step-up multiples for the stage and the representativeness of any broader Defense & Security peer set. Refinement would require either (1) closer comparable visibility at identical stage and capital-raise profile, or (2) explicit revenue or margin data to support alternative methodologies.
